front_blocks.md: Define **acid rain**.

back_blocks.md: **Acid rain** is precipitation that has become **acidic** because **sulfur dioxide** and **nitrogen oxides** react with water and oxygen in the atmosphere to form acids.

front_blocks.md: What is the main source of **sulfur dioxide** emissions?

back_blocks.md: **Power stations** that burn coal and oil are the main source of sulfur dioxide emissions.

cards.front_md: What is the main source of **sulfur dioxide** emissions?
cards.back_md: **Power stations** that burn coal and oil are the main source of sulfur dioxide emissions.

front_blocks.md: Nitrogen oxides form when atmospheric nitrogen reacts with oxygen at the very high <u>                </u> inside engines and furnaces.

back_blocks.md: Nitrogen oxides form when atmospheric nitrogen reacts with oxygen at the very high **temperatures** inside engines and furnaces.

front_blocks.md: Where do most **nitrogen oxide** emissions come from?

back_blocks.md: Most nitrogen oxide emissions come from **vehicle exhausts**.

cards.front_md: Where do most **nitrogen oxide** emissions come from?

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
All the gases that cause acid rain come from human activities.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
**Natural sources**, such as **volcanic eruptions**, also release the gases that cause acid rain.

front_blocks.md: Define **dry deposition**.

back_blocks.md: **Dry deposition** is when acidic gases settle directly onto surfaces such as buildings, vegetation and soil **without rain**.

cards.front_md: Define **dry deposition**.

front_blocks.md: How does acid rain affect the **pH** of lakes and rivers?

back_blocks.md: Acid rain **lowers the pH** of lakes and rivers, causing **water acidification** that can leave them unable to support life.

cards.front_md: How does acid rain affect the **pH** of lakes and rivers?
cards.back_md: Acid rain **lowers the pH** of lakes and rivers, causing **water acidification** that can leave them unable to support life.

front_blocks.md: Why does **acidification** of a lake lead to the death of larger fish?

back_blocks.md: Acidification kills the **microorganisms** at the base of the **food web**, so the food supply for larger fish dwindles.

cards.front_md: Why does **acidification** of a lake lead to the death of larger fish?
cards.back_md: Acidification kills the **microorganisms** at the base of the **food web**, so the food supply for larger fish dwindles.

front_blocks.md: Acid rain can <u>      </u> aluminium, copper and other heavy metals out of the soil and into runoff and drinking water.

back_blocks.md: Acid rain can **leach** aluminium, copper and other heavy metals out of the soil and into runoff and drinking water.

front_blocks.md: Define **transboundary pollution**.

back_blocks.md: **Transboundary pollution** is pollution that winds carry across national borders, so acid rain falls on countries **downwind** of the source.

cards.front_md: Define **transboundary pollution**.
cards.back_md: **Transboundary pollution** is pollution that winds carry across national borders, so acid rain falls on countries **downwind** of the source.

front_blocks.md: How does acid rain affect **soil nutrients**?

back_blocks.md: Acid rain **lowers soil pH**, which **reduces the nutrients** in the soil and makes it harder for plants to absorb nutrients and grow.

cards.front_md: How does acid rain affect **soil nutrients**?
cards.back_md: Acid rain **lowers soil pH**, which **reduces the nutrients** in the soil and makes it harder for plants to absorb nutrients and grow.

front_blocks.md: How does acid rain falling on **leaves** damage a plant?

back_blocks.md: Acid rain damages the leaves' **protective waxy coating**, which interrupts **water and gas exchange** and can eventually kill the plant.

cards.front_md: How does acid rain falling on **leaves** damage a plant?
cards.back_md: Acid rain damages the leaves' **protective waxy coating**, which interrupts **water and gas exchange** and can eventually kill the plant.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Coniferous trees such as pine and spruce withstand acid rain well.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Conifers are especially vulnerable to acid rain because of their **shallow root systems** and **thin bark**.

front_blocks.md: Why does acid rain damage **limestone** and **marble** buildings?

back_blocks.md: Limestone and marble contain **calcium carbonate**, which reacts with sulfuric or nitric acid, so the stone **corrodes and weakens**.

cards.front_md: Why does acid rain damage **limestone** and **marble** buildings?

front_blocks.md: Why do soils in **Sweden** become acidic so easily?

back_blocks.md: Swedish soils become acidic easily because they contain **very little limestone**.

front_blocks.md: Define **flue gas desulfurisation**.

back_blocks.md: **Flue gas desulfurisation** is a process that removes **sulfur dioxide** from the waste gases of coal-fired power stations before they leave the chimney.

cards.front_md: Define **flue gas desulfurisation**.
cards.back_md: **Flue gas desulfurisation** is a process that removes **sulfur dioxide** from the waste gases of coal-fired power stations before they leave the chimney.

front_blocks.md: What does a **flue gas desulfurisation** scrubber spray over the waste gases?

back_blocks.md: The scrubber sprays a **wet slurry** of **calcium oxide** and **calcium carbonate** over the waste gases.

cards.front_md: What does a **flue gas desulfurisation** scrubber spray over the waste gases?
cards.back_md: The scrubber sprays a **wet slurry** of **calcium oxide** and **calcium carbonate** over the waste gases.

front_blocks.md: Why can the gas leaving a **desulfurisation absorber** damage equipment?

back_blocks.md: The gas is **highly corrosive** because it is saturated with water and still contains some sulfur dioxide.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Using **corrosion-resistant materials** or **reheating the gases** above dew point reduces corrosion but **adds to the running costs** of the system.

front_blocks.md: Define **catalytic converter**.

back_blocks.md: A **catalytic converter** is a device fitted to a vehicle's exhaust that uses **metal catalysts** to convert toxic gases, such as nitrogen oxides and carbon monoxide, into less toxic gases.

front_blocks.md: Why do the catalysts in a **catalytic converter** sit in a **honeycomb**?

back_blocks.md: The honeycomb **increases the surface area** available for the reactions.

cards.front_md: Why do the catalysts in a **catalytic converter** sit in a **honeycomb**?

front_blocks.md: Why can a **catalytic converter** increase a vehicle's fuel consumption?

back_blocks.md: A catalytic converter can increase fuel consumption because the engine needs **extra fuel** to keep the converter **hot enough to work**.

back_blocks.md: Carpooling offers **limited flexibility** and causes extra **wear and tear** on vehicles, which raises maintenance costs.
